`npm run feed:import` fetched 1,842 advisories over 19 pages and mapped 4,782 IOCs, of which 4,549 were already in the feed and 64 already covered by a bare-name entry.
**169 new entries written, 122 corroborated against OSV.dev.** All npm.
Nothing was reported unmappable, no page cap was hit, and nothing was left waiting behind `--limit` (169 is under the 250 default), so the next run starts from a clean window.

- **Eleven fake concurrency primitives**, published as a set: `mutex-forge`, `keyed-mutex-map`, `single-flight-lock`, `semaphore-job-pool`, `priority-mutex-lane`, `shared-slot-gate`, `resource-lease-pool`, `lock-deadline-guard`, `try-lock-runner`, `async-lock-queue`, `async-critical-section`.

- **AI and agent tooling**: `ai-analyzer` (20 versions, the largest single package this window), `cc-skills-helper`, `@kolbo/mcp`, `xrblocks-mcp`, `mastraqqq`, `nolimit-agent` with its `@nolimit-agent/linux-x64` and `@nolimit-agent/win32-x64` platform binaries.

- **Dependency-confusion placeholders at sentinel versions**: the `@hzero-front-ui` scope (five packages) and `fr-ito-web-react` at `99.99.99`, the `@khaznatech` scope at `99.0.0`, and `@dgn-src-click-to-pay-org/srcdcfreleasecert` at `374.0.0`.
59 of the 169 are bare names rather than version pins, which is the shape that would hurt if one of them were an established package.
Every one was checked against the npm registry; the result is under "Bare-name blocks" below.

As a first pass, twelve of the riskiest-looking (`react-shield`, `source-analyzer`, `root-locator`, `path-match-js`, `ts-enum-helper`, `mutex-forge`, `sourceflow-tracker`, `finvu-hdfc-sdk`, `blocks-angular`, `index-design-system`, `lab-helper`, `nolimit-agent`) were each created 2026-08-13 with a single published version.
`nolimit-agent` is the outlier worth noting: 12,272 downloads in 30 days off a one-day-old single-version package.

primary.body:
Daily threat-intel sweep for 2026-08-14, released as v5.26.2. The sweep was prepared first and the release folded into the same PR, so there is one merge and one CI settle before the tag; the release detail is at the foot.

## Importer

`npm run feed:import` fetched 1,842 advisories over 19 pages and mapped 4,782 IOCs, of which 4,549 were already in the feed and 64 already covered by a bare-name entry. **169 new entries written, 122 corroborated against OSV.dev.** All npm.

Nothing was reported unmappable, no page cap was hit, and nothing was left waiting behind `--limit` (169 is under the 250 default), so the next run starts from a clean window.

### What is in the 169

- **Eleven fake concurrency primitives**, published as a set: `mutex-forge`, `keyed-mutex-map`, `single-flight-lock`, `semaphore-job-pool`, `priority-mutex-lane`, `shared-slot-gate`, `resource-lease-pool`, `lock-deadline-guard`, `try-lock-runner`, `async-lock-queue`, `async-critical-section`.
- **Crypto-library typosquats**, version-pinned: `@solana-js/web3@1.91.3`, `@ethers-js/contracts@6.9.0`, `@opezneppelin/contracts@5.0.2`, plus `bs58-15`, `bs58-33`, `bs58-77`.
- **A date-formatting typosquat family**: `datefmt-util-helper`, `datetime-format-xutil`, `datetime-fmt-xutil`, `date-fmt-utils-helper`, `date-fmt-helper-xz`, `fmt-util-k7x2`.
- **Assert-library impersonations**: `js-assert-plus`, `minimalistic-assert-plus`, `power-assert-plus`, `chai-as-reformed`.
- **AI and agent tooling**: `ai-analyzer` (20 versions, the largest single package this window), `cc-skills-helper`, `@kolbo/mcp`, `xrblocks-mcp`, `mastraqqq`, `nolimit-agent` with its `@nolimit-agent/linux-x64` and `@nolimit-agent/win32-x64` platform binaries.
- **Dependency-confusion placeholders at sentinel versions**: the `@hzero-front-ui` scope (five packages) and `fr-ito-web-react` at `99.99.99`, the `@khaznatech` scope at `99.0.0`, and `@dgn-src-click-to-pay-org/srcdcfreleasecert` at `374.0.0`.

### False-positive review

59 of the 169 are bare names rather than version pins, which is the shape that would hurt if one of them were an established package. Every one was checked against the npm registry; the result is under "Bare-name blocks" below. As a first pass, twelve of the riskiest-looking (`react-shield`, `source-analyzer`, `root-locator`, `path-match-js`, `ts-enum-helper`, `mutex-forge`, `sourceflow-tracker`, `finvu-hdfc-sdk`, `blocks-angular`, `index-design-system`, `lab-helper`, `nolimit-agent`) were each created 2026-08-13 with a single published version. `nolimit-agent` is the outlier worth noting: 12,272 downloads in 30 days off a one-day-old single-version package.

## Manual enrichment

None this run, which is itself the finding. Every campaign the vendor sweep surfaced is already fully covered, re-checked against the current blocklist:

- **ChainDrop / keyv** (2026-08-04): the `npm-cache[.]com` domain and the `StringListStore` contract address are both present.
- **Miasma "Hades"**: covered by #140 yesterday.

The four DNS-fallback subdomains `sdk[.]`, `ext[.]`, `pkg[.]` and `net[.]dl[.]wel1[.]ru` are covered by the single `dl[.]wel1[.]ru` entry rather than listed individually, which `campaigns.test.ts:4029` asserts.

## Verification

`npm run build` is green (all seven governance gates, `check:feed`, `check:handoff`, `tsc`).

The two failures in `campaigns.test.ts` are the known Windows `IOC_KNOWN_C2_DOMAIN` gap (Phantom Bot and GlassWASM delivery host); both were re-run on unmodified `main` and fail identically there, so they are the environment and not a regression. **CI runs the full suite on this PR and that is the authoritative verdict.**

No pattern tables were touched, so no regex-shape risk in this change.

## Release v5.26.2

This PR now also carries the release. PATCH: feed data only, no new rule and no change to what the scanner does, same call as v5.26.1. Version bumped at all 14 `versionSites` plus the lockfile, `feed.json` and the handoff set regenerated, and `NEXT_ACTIONS.md` moved to v5.26.2.

### Bare-name blocks: resolved, all 59 stay as names

The question was whether the bare names under corporate-looking scopes (`@rocketreach`, `@sapappgyver`, `@open-banking`, `@stockrepublic`, `@sourceflow-uk`, `@hanssoft`) were hijacked legitimate packages that ought to be version-pinned. They were not.

All 60 bare names were queried against the npm registry. 59 now carry exactly one version, `0.0.1-security`, published by the `npm-support` account: npm's takedown stub, which npm publishes only when it removes a name in its entirety. The single exception, `@dsp-next-gen-ui/needs-review`, carries that stub plus the malicious dependency-confusion sentinel `999.99.1`, and no legitimate release either.

The marker discriminates, which is what makes it usable rather than merely suggestive. Against genuinely hijacked packages as controls, `keyv` (85 versions, `lukechilds`/`jaredwray`), `flat-cache` (52, `jaredwray`) and `axios` (143, `jasonsaayman`) are all intact with full version history, because npm removed the bad versions and left the name with its real owner. A whole-name takedown therefore means the name was attacker-owned end to end, and a version pin would be wrong since no legitimate version survives to preserve.

### Verification

`npm run build` green on the release commit: seven governance gates, `check:feed`, `check:handoff` (which correctly caught the stale `NEXT_ACTIONS.md` version header before the commit), and `tsc`.

Locally: `reporter`, `cli`, `feed`, `threat-intel`, `ioc-blocklist`, `feed-import`, `sbom-generator`, `issue-54-hardening` - 298 passed, 1 skipped. CI runs the full suite here and is the authoritative verdict.
